name: Primary Pulmonary Lymphoma

criteria.description: Lymphomatous infiltration confined to lung parenchyma with or without hilar/mediastinal lymph node involvement, without extrapulmonary disease at diagnosis
Histopathological confirmation of lymphoma subtype by biopsy of lung tissue
Exclusion of systemic lymphoma or secondary pulmonary involvement by imaging and bone marrow biopsy
Immunophenotypic characterization supporting B-cell or T-cell lymphoma subtype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: lung-confined disease, histopathological confirmation, and exclusion of systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including radiology, pathology, and clinical correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent localized pulmonary infiltrates on imaging
searchTerms: lung spots or patches that don’t clear on scans
persistent lung infiltrates seen on imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Primary lung mass or nodules without systemic lymphadenopathy
searchTerms: lung mass or nodules without swollen lymph nodes
primary lung tumor without lymph node enlargement

occasional.symptomName: Chest discomfort or pleuritic chest pain

searchTerms: immune system attacks related to cancer

laboratory: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: Chest CT showing solitary or multiple pulmonary nodules or masses
Absence of widespread lymphadenopathy or extrapulmonary lesions
genetic: Clonal B-cell receptor gene rearrangements in B-cell PPL
Chromosomal abnormalities such as t(11;18)(q21;q21) in MALT lymphoma subtype
other: Histopathology demonstrating lymphoid infiltrates with immunophenotyping confirming lymphoma subtype

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic lymphoma with secondary lung involvement
Presence of infectious agents on microbiological studies
Lack of clonal lymphoid infiltrates on biopsy
Different radiologic patterns such as spiculated masses

redFlags: Persistent unexplained pulmonary infiltrates despite treatment
Development of systemic symptoms such as night sweats and significant weight loss
references: Cordier JF, Chailleux E, Lauque D, et al. Primary pulmonary lymphomas. A clinical study of 70 cases in nonimmunocompromised patients. Chest. 1993;103(1):201-208.
Cadranel J, Wislez M, Antoine M. Primary pulmonary lymphoma. Eur Respir J. 2002;20(3):750-762.
Koss MN, Hochholzer L, Nichols PW, Wehunt WD, Lazarus AA. Primary non-Hodgkin's lymphoma of the lung: a clinicopathologic study of 27 cases. Cancer. 1983;51(6):951-958.
